This seem to duplicate a lot of code from `RemovedFiles.test.js`. Maybe it makes sense to merge both files into one.

so one of the issues I ran into was that the initial watchRun hook was being called before `watcher` was assigned, and it would throw an error at `watcher.close()`. In fact, if you look at the original code, `done()` is being called before `watcher.close()`, and I realized that it pretty much just hides the error, because the test succeed before the error can be thrown
this is a good point, I will merge them into a `ChangesAndRemovals.test.js` file

This first comment still makes sense, because you should not assume that watchRun is called synchrously in `.watch`.

Maybe it even makes sense to wait for compilation completion before ending the test. `close()` has a callback that is called when the watcher has closed: `watch.close(done)`.
